title: Obesity, morbid obesity and BMI
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's weight diagnosis and BMI, if reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for weight management.

Vitals: BP 140/88, HR 76, SpO2 96% on room air, BMI 52.8.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for mild knee pain during exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits.

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is an 83-year-old male presenting for evaluation of significant weight gain and associated mobility issues. He reports difficulty walking long distances and experiences shortness of breath during moderate physical activity. He expresses a desire to lose weight to improve his quality of life.

Assessment:
1. Morbid obesity.

Plan:
Discussed the risks associated with his current weight and the importance of weight reduction. Provided education on caloric intake and encouraged increased daily activity as tolerated. I have provided a referral to a formal weight management program for structured support. Patient will follow up in four weeks to monitor progress.

Medication List:
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Electronically signed,
M. Okafor, MD
October 14, 2026
explanations: Morbid (severe) obesity documented by the provider: E66.01 (HCC 48).
BMI 52.x with a provider weight diagnosis: add Z68.43 (BMI 40 or more maps to HCC 48 on its own).

distractors.why: The provider documents morbid obesity: E66.01, not E66.9.
The BMI is documented and the provider diagnosed the weight condition: add the Z68 code.
